title: Reporting, Metrics and Assurance
summary: The information boards need to oversee resilience and cyber risk, how to read dashboards critically and how to obtain credible independent assurance rather than relying on assertion.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The information boards need to oversee resilience and cyber risk, how to read dashboards critically and how to obtain credible independent assurance rather than relying on assertion.
Learning Objectives: Specify the management information and indicators the board needs
Interpret resilience and cyber reports and identify what is missing
Obtain independent assurance from internal audit and external reviewers
Syllabus: The core board information set: services, tolerances, incidents and remediation
Key risk indicators: patching, privileged access, backups and third parties
Recognising comfort without evidence and green dashboards
Internal audit, external testing and certifications as assurance
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members, especially on risk, audit and technology committees
Executive directors and senior managers accountable for operations, technology, security and resilience
Company secretaries and heads of governance supporting board oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No technical background in technology or cyber security is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for Operational Resilience (2021)
FSB, Effective Practices for Cyber Incident Response and Recovery (2020)
FSB, Enhancing Third-Party Risk Management and Oversight: A Toolkit for Financial Institutions and Financial Authorities (2023)
